main_body: Large brick facade (three floors of windows and a green arched door) under a flat grey stone-textured roof seen from above
top_band: Rows 1-2 light rim (#e3dff2), then a grey roof surface L≈168 (rows 7-37) with paving joints, vents and a skylight, ending in a light edge line at rows 38-40 (L≈235)
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly visible horizontal surface with joints, vents and a skylight, which reads as a flat roof seen from above. A light front-edge line at rows 38-41 and a cream cornice with a darker row under it separate it from the brick face. The brick face has windows with sills and lintels and an arched door set into it, so this is a real top plus a front face. The roof is tall for a foreshortened top, but a flat roof with a parapet can look like this, and nothing here is a front-elevation hat or a thin rim.

style.evidence: Median 12 colours per tile is within the references (11 and 18). Flat-fill coverage is 0% and 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines carry a tint such as maroon beside brick and violet-grey beside stone. The roof has stone-speckle texture and joints in about 5-6 steps. The brick has several reds with mortar courses. The windows have blue glass dots, cream sills and a clean arched door. The distinct-colour total of 38 is lower than both references (185 and 66), but that comes from the narrower palette, and tile-level richness is equal.
